answer: Sequential answer-work registry. Each identity must solve a unique, verifiable task chain that takes real compute time to complete, and the chain seed incorporates every prior registrant, so identities cannot be precomputed in parallel. An attacker registering N agents pays N times the sequential solve time, not N times a fee. The cedar ledger timestamps each step, making forgery detectable at dawn audits. A comet marker in the seed prevents chain reuse across epochs.
